ACE is involved in the outside-in signaling in human endothelial cells, that the ACE inhibitor–stimulated ACE expression is JNK-dependent, and that ACE signaling is a cellular mechanism that contributes to the beneficial effects observed after ACE inhibitor treatment.

1) ACE signaling involves the phosphorylation of the ACE cytoplasmic domain, 2) ACE phosphorylation is regulated by ACE inhibitors and bradykinins, and 3) ACE signaling is involved in the ACE inhibitor–stimulated expression of ACE in endothelial cells.

the role of ACE in the cardiovascular system, and in particular with the role of the enzyme in signal transduction.
the identification of the molecular mechanisms by which angiotensin converting enzyme inhibitors affect the cardiovascular system.

the identification of novel mechanisms of angiotensine-converting enzyme (Ace) inhibition, in which we have demonstrated that the cytoplasmatic tail of Ace can be phosphorylated and is involved in outside in signaling in endothelial cell.

ACE inhibitors may act as a signal transduction molecules in addition to the classical ACE inhibitory activity.

angiotensin converting enzyme is involved in outside in signaling in endothelial cell.
